# 09 · The Fenwick Family: What Each Person Knows (SEALED)

> The heart of the campaign. Use this before any family scene.

## Ash's keepsake: the split locket (SEC-23, CHG-06)
- **What Ash carries:** a dented pewter half-locket on a leather cord under his shirt. Front: a worn crest, a river ford with antlers above it. Inside, behind cracked glass, a curl of baby hair and a scratched "A." The hinge is broken off on one side.
- **What Ash believes:** it was his mother's. Gideon gave it to him when he was ten and said, "That was Mum's. That's your hair in it. The other half was lost in the fire." (All true. Gideon just doesn't say whose neck the other half was on.) Ash has pawned everything he owns at least once. He's never pawned this, and he's never quite been able to say why. Sometimes it goes cold for no reason.
- **What Gideon and Zeke know:** the other half was Wren's, with her curl in it. They think it went into the river with her.
- **Truth:** see 00-core-truths §4 and SEC-23. Clara wears the matching back half.

## The family secrets (layered reveals)

### Layer 1: "You had a twin." (SEC-16)
- **What Gideon and Zeke know:** they had a baby sister, Wren, Ash's twin. Everyone believed she died in the fire; her body was never found ("the river took her").
- **Why they never told Ash:** Gideon decided at 14, raising a toddler, that Ash would grow up without a ghost. He made Zeke promise. Zeke has hated that promise for years. **The Fringe's oldest neighbors know too** and have kept quiet out of respect for Gideon.
- **Seeds:**
  1. Every Turn of Light (Ash's birthday), Gideon floats **three** lamps on the river: "Mum, Dad, and one for luck."
  2. A second tiny cradle under a sheet in the attic, next to Zeke's workshop junk. Zeke won't let Ash use it for parts.
  3. An old neighbor slips: "You've got your mother's eyes, the both of— ah, the eyes, I mean."
  4. Zeke flinches when anyone says "Wren."
  5. The old lullaby has two verses, one with each baby's name. Zeke knows both.
- **Reveal:** Act I, after Ash starts hearing the call and Moss's first explanations. Gideon or Zeke tells him. It's a family scene, not a plot dump. Big fight, then reconciliation.

### Layer 2: "She's alive." (SEC-03)
- Revealed later (Act I end / Act II). The campaign file sets exact chapter and routes.
- **Seeds:** see 00-core-truths §4. Also: Clara's birthday is Midsummer's Eve; Hollis says she came to him "as a little one, the autumn of the bad fires"; she hums the lullaby's tune (first verse only) while working at the Lamplit.

### Layer 3: "Moss carried you out." (SEC-01, SEC-09)
- Gideon's memory of the antlered shape is his private shame. He thinks it was a shock dream, and he never trusted Moss fully because of it (an unease he can't explain). When Moss is revealed, Gideon's reaction is the strongest: he has to choose to trust the thing he's half-feared for 19 years.

### Layer 4: "Hollis ordered it." (SEC-04)
- Zeke's devastation: his scholarship benefactor and hero. This can be a mid-to-late reveal.

| Zeke | **Yes** | No | No (finds Moss "interesting") | No | No |
| Moss | Yes | **No** (believes Wren died) | Yes | Yes | No (suspects "someone in the city" from the Calm's stink in still water, doesn't know who) |
| Clara | No | — | No | No (doesn't know her own) | No |
| Hollis | Took her | Yes (his ward) | No (has heard rumors of "a stag at the ford") | **No.** Believes the only heir is Clara. | Yes |
| Old neighbors | Yes | No | Notice he never ages | No | No |

## The brothers' life at campaign start (player-safe version will go in the packet)
- They own the leaning house at the bottom of Willow Lane.
- Money is always short. Gideon's guard and bouncer work pays the house tax. Zeke's tuition comes and goes; the Enchanters' Guild scholarship has paid twice.
- Gideon tries to rein Ash in. Ash sneaks out by the roof hatch. Zeke covers for Ash half the time and lectures him the other half.
- Gideon calls everyone by full names: "Asheron." "Ezekiel." "Margery." Ash hates "Asheron." Only the brothers use it.
- Restday supper is sacred. All three eat together, often with Moss.
